name: Agag
description: King living at the time of United Monarchy

points: And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword. Wait, what did King Saul do?

Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until thou comest to Shur, and utterly destroyed the people with the edge of the sword; but he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive. He halfway fulfilled the order, reasoning like the king might be valuable as a hostage, as if the Lord forgot that detail.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them; but every thing that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly. They killed what looked like it deserved killing, so they could say they did some killing, and kept the healthy, good looking animals, telling themselves surely the Lord could not have meant these.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.

Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the Lord? Saul answered, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek. Wait a minute: the king is still alive. Saul is playing the defensive, justifying his actions, making excuses.

Saul is in denial: Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites. Samuel breaks down the rebuke and Saul tells the prophet he is wrong.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. Agag came unto him delicately, crouching and speaking softly, and Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Agag came delicately, thinking the king had spared him.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately, and said, Surely the bitterness of death is past; with Saul under rebuke, Agag figured nobody was mad at the Amalekites anymore and he was safe.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal. The old prophet did not play; he finished the commandment himself, measure for measure for what Amalek's sword had done.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

points: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. Sound familiar? This is a descendant of the same Agag that Samuel hewed in pieces. Haman is an Amalekite, an Edomite, and the king set his seat above all the princes: the right hand of the king over Persia.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite: Agag was the Amalekite king of 1 Samuel 15, so Haman descended from the Edomites Saul failed to finish, and when he learned Mordecai was of Saul's line he sought to kill them all. From the womb to the tomb, this is war.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

points: After these things the king promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite and set his seat above all the princes, and all the king's servants in the king's gate bowed and reverenced him, for the king had so commanded, but Mordecai bowed not nor did him reverence.

note.label: Esther 3: Haman the Agagite and the Decree to Destroy the Jews

points: Esther fell down at the king's feet and besought him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite and the device he had devised against the Jews.

note.label: Esther 8: The Decree Reversed for the Jews

points: The Jews undertook to keep what Mordecai wrote, because Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite had devised against the Jews to destroy them and had cast Pur, that is the lot, to consume them.

note.label: Esther 9: Purim and the Victory of the Jews
